chapter: Touring, recording and Fletcher's band in the 1940s
title: North Carolina warehouse dance and fan mail from WBBM
summary: In North Carolina the band played a mixed audience in a warehouse with a portable floor and the bus inside. Horace weighed fan mail from the powerful WBBM to choose one-nighter routes.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: not -- we played a warehouse, in the warehouse, and they had one of these kind of floors that you put in -- dance floors just for this particular case. Now what do you call that?
: Portable floor, I don't -- That's the word I wanted,

(Unaudible) and this was a mixed audience, and we would drive the bus -- we had a bus at that time that we could rent, you know, and we could drive the bus right up into the warehouse, you know, right next to the --

And unload, right in there, and when we'd take our intermission, the guys want to go sit in the bus, right there, and you still -- overhead you're covered. And the people would pay $2.50 and $3.00 and a half a head to get in. And you talking about some dances, and some of them were really comedians dancing, you know. And a lot of people, they had grandstands, like sections in the baseball games, you know, outdoors. And a lot of the people didn't dance, but they would come to observe, and they would see some funny things, and, of course, they would listen to the band. And we played quite a few of those.
you said WBBM in Chicago -- Yes. Yes.
-- which was a pretty powerful station, wasn't it?

Yes, I used to get quite a bit of fan mail from all over in that section. And I used to weigh the fan mail and see how much I had from different -- from how many states and what not. This is how we would figure out our best one nighters. This is the way we'd do it, and it would pay off that way, you see. We'd get quite a bit of fan mail.
